scenes.heading: Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
scenes.narration: Terraform lets you define your cloud infrastructure as code, so provisioning becomes declarative, versioned, and repeatable.

scenes.heading: Core Terraform ideas
bullets: Declarative: describe the desired end state
Providers connect to clouds and services
scenes.narration: Terraform is declarative, meaning you describe the end state you want rather than the steps to get there. Providers are plugins that let it talk to clouds like AWS or services like Snowflake. The plan command previews exactly what will change before anything happens. And a state file records what Terraform has actually created so it can reconcile future changes.

scenes.heading: Provisioning a data bucket
scenes.narration: The terraform block pins the AWS provider to a compatible version so builds stay reproducible. The first resource declares an S3 bucket to serve as a data lake. The second resource enables versioning on that same bucket, and notice how it references the first resource by its address, letting Terraform figure out the correct order to create them.

scenes.heading: The Terraform workflow
scenes.narration: You start with init, which downloads the providers your configuration needs. Then plan computes the difference between your code and the real world. You review that diff carefully to confirm the intended changes. Finally apply executes the plan and updates both your infrastructure and the state file.

scenes.heading: Click-ops vs Terraform
scenes.narration: Clicking around in a cloud console leaves changes undocumented, hard to roll back, and prone to configuration drift. Terraform routes every change through code review, makes environments reproducible, and shows you a precise diff before you commit to applying it.

scenes.text: Terraform makes infrastructure reproducible: describe the desired state, review the plan, then apply with confidence.
scenes.narration: The core value of Terraform is reproducible infrastructure: you describe the desired state, review the plan, and then apply it with confidence.
